query: Prior calculations on concentrated alloys examined variations in atomic mass and force constants, temperature-dependent lattice heat transport, or DFT-derived elastic properties coupled to analytical conductivity estimates; some estimates require a Debye temperature. The cited simulations generally represented perfect, defect-free bulk crystals. Experiments below 200 K indicate that lattice and electronic contributions in HfNbTaTiZr can be comparable, while measurements from 300 to 1200 K on a specimen containing 1 wt.% oxygen report total conductivity of 10–17 W/(K m). Available analytical approaches do not capture all relevant atomic-scale complexity in refractory high-entropy alloys, and separate transport studies do not establish a predictive solution for this alloy. Given these constraints, what testable hypothesis could an unspecified new predictive approach make for HfNbTaTiZr without conflating lattice and electronic heat transport? Explain why it should outperform earlier approaches, quantify the expected improvement, define its temperature and sample applicability limits, identify supporting observations from the cited work, and specify decisive comparisons with low- and high-temperature measurements that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: A newly developed multi‐scale predictive model that explicitly decouples lattice from electronic heat transport in defect‐free HfNbTaTiZr will predict that the lattice thermal conductivity is lower than previous Debye or naïve DFT-based estimates (by roughly 20–40% in accuracy improvement) while also capturing the crossover regime below 200 K where lattice and electronic contributions are comparable.
generation.material_initial_state: Defect‐free, high-purity bulk HfNbTaTiZr alloy (with optionally controlled low oxygen content, e.g., below 1 wt.% in comparison specimens).
generation.intervention: Application of an integrated computational approach combining density-functional theory for accurate electronic structure, refined lattice dynamics methods incorporating disorder-induced mass and force-constant fluctuations, and Boltzmann transport calculations that separately address phonon scattering and electron conduction.
generation.conditions: Predictions are to be compared under isothermal conditions spanning low temperatures (<200 K, where lattice and electronic contributions are comparable) and high temperatures (300–1200 K) in inert or otherwise controlled atmospheres.
generation.structural_mediator: Atomic-scale disorder (i.e., variations in atomic mass and force-constant distributions) that modifies phonon lifetimes and dispersion, thereby reducing lattice thermal conductivity relative to simpler analytical models.
generation.mechanism: By decoupling the transport channels, the model separately calculates (a) a reduced lattice thermal conductivity due to enhanced phonon scattering from local disorder and (b) an independently determined electronic contribution. This segregation avoids the overestimation inherent in approaches that conflate the two contributions, leading to more reliable predictions especially in the low-temperature regime.
generation.predicted_outcome: The new approach will predict lower lattice thermal conductivity than previously estimated (by a margin that should translate into an overall improvement in predictive accuracy by approximately 20–40%), along with distinct temperature dependencies for the lattice and electronic contributions. In particular, below 200 K, the model should clarify a crossover behavior where lattice and electronic thermal conductivities are nearly equal.
generation.baseline: Earlier analytical and conventional DFT-based estimates that use a Debye temperature approximation and do not separately account for disorder effects on phonon scattering, often leading to conflated or overestimated thermal conductivity values.
generation.boundary: The predictions are applicable to bulk, defect-free HfNbTaTiZr in the temperature range from roughly 50 K (where quantum effects are significant) up to 1200 K. Deviations may occur in samples with significant oxygen contamination or other defects beyond 1 wt.%, or in microstructures that are not homogeneous.
generation.uncertainty: Although the approach is expected to outperform earlier methods, the exact quantitative improvement in predictive accuracy (e.g., the precise percentage reduction in lattice thermal conductivity estimates or error margins) remains uncertain without direct experimental calibration, especially in the low-temperature crossover regime.

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize high-purity, defect-free HfNbTaTiZr samples and perform detailed thermal conductivity measurements over a temperature range from ~50 K to 1200 K. Use complementary techniques—such as time-domain thermoreflectance to probe lattice thermal conductivity and terahertz spectroscopy for electronic conductivity—to independently quantify each contribution.
measurements: Lattice thermal conductivity (via phonon lifetime and dispersion measurements)
Electronic thermal conductivity (using electron scattering time analysis)
Comparison of predicted vs. experimental crossover behavior below 200 K
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis will be falsified if the experimental data do not show separately identifiable and distinct temperature-dependence for the lattice and electronic contributions, or if the overall predictive accuracy does not improve by at least approximately 20% compared to conventional Debye-based or conflated DFT models.

Low-frequency conductivity of low wear high-entropy alloys

Abstract: High-entropy alloys (HEAs) provide new research avenues for alloy combinations in the periodic table, opening numerous possibilities in novel-alloy applications. However, their electrical characteristics have been relatively underexplored. The challenge in establishing an HEA electrical conductivity model lies in the changes in electronic characteristics caused by lattice distortion and complexity of nanostructures. Here we show a low-frequency electrical conductivity model for the Nb-Mo-Ta-W HEA system. The cocktail effect is found to explain trends in electrical-conductivity changes in HEAs, while the magnitude of the reduction is understood by the calculated plasma frequency, free electron density, and measured relaxation time by terahertz spectroscopy. As a result, the refractory HEA Nb15Mo35Ta15W35 thin film exhibits both high hardness and excellent conductivity. This combination of Nb15Mo35Ta15W35 makes it suitable for applications in atomic force microscopy probe coating, significantly improving their wear resistance and atomic-scale image resolution. Phonon behavior in a random solid solution: a lattice dynamics study on the high-entropy alloy FeCoCrMnNi

Abstract: AbstractHigh-Entropy Alloys (HEAs) are a new family of crystalline random alloys with four or more elements in a simple unit cell, at the forefront of materials research for their exceptional mechanical properties. Their strong chemical disorder leads to mass and force-constant fluctuations which are expected to strongly reduce phonon lifetime, responsible for thermal transport, similarly to glasses. Still, the long range order would associate HEAs to crystals with a complex disordered unit cell. These two families of materials, however, exhibit very different phonon dynamics, still leading to similar thermal properties. The question arises on the positioning of HEAs in this context. Here we present an exhaustive experimental investigation of the lattice dynamics in a HEA, Fe20Co20Cr20Mn20Ni20, using inelastic neutron and X-ray scattering. We demonstrate that HEAs present unique phonon dynamics at the frontier between fully disordered and ordered materials, characterized by long-propagating acoustic phonons in the whole Brillouin zone.Subject terms: Electronic proper

Investigation of PbSnTeSe High-Entropy Thermoelectric Alloy: A DFT Approach

Abstract: Thermoelectric materials have attracted extensive attention because they can directly convert waste heat into electric energy. As a brand-new method of alloying, high-entropy alloys (HEAs) have attracted much attention in the fields of materials science and engineering. Recent researches have found that HEAs could be potentially good thermoelectric (TE) materials. In this study, special quasi-random structures (SQS) of PbSnTeSe high-entropy alloys consisting of 64 atoms have been generated. The thermoelectric transport properties of the highest-entropy PbSnTeSe-optimized structure were investigated by combining calculations from first-principles density-functional theory and on-the-fly machine learning with the semiclassical Boltzmann transport theory and Green–Kubo theory. The results demonstrate that PbSnTeSe HEA has a very low lattice thermal conductivity. The electrical conductivity, thermal electronic conductivity and Seebeck coefficient have been evaluated for both n-type and p-type doping.
